symbols.name: chirp value
symbols.meaning: The chirp value $\chi_\alpha=\exp(-\pi i \alpha^2/q)$ at an integer $\alpha$.
symbols.quote: Let $\chi_\alpha=\exp(-\pi i \alpha^2/q)$ be the chirp value at an integer $\alpha$, the chirp index here.

symbols.name: chirp index
symbols.meaning: An integer at which a chirp or phase value is evaluated.
symbols.quote: Let $\chi_\alpha=\exp(-\pi i \alpha^2/q)$ be the chirp value at an integer $\alpha$, the chirp index here.

symbols.name: phase twist
symbols.meaning: The phase factor $\tau_\alpha=\exp(\pi i \alpha/q)$ at an integer $\alpha$, which changes sign when $\alpha$ increases by $q$.
symbols.quote: Let $\tau_\alpha=\exp(\pi i \alpha/q)$ be the phase twist at an integer $\alpha$, which satisfies $\tau_{\alpha+q}=-\tau_\alpha$.

relations.quote: Bluestein's chirp identity rewrites the [discrete Fourier transform](fourier-transform.md) of a vector and computes it by a [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) placed between two pointwise multiplications.

Bluestein's chirp identity rewrites the [discrete Fourier transform](fourier-transform.md) of a vector and computes it by a [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) placed between two pointwise multiplications.
Bluestein's chirp identity acts on the middle transform of the paper's multiplication algorithm, including its [target permutation](gaussian-resampling.md).
